affected_boundaries: JSON source dialect and configured executable source kind

observed_behavior: JSON dispatch dropped an existing JSONC comment unit and rejected a configured executable JSON integration Arc.
expected_behavior: Preserve existing JSONC annotations and discover canonical JSON test annotations according to the configured source kind.
causal_mechanism: Extension dispatch assumed every .json source was strict implementation configuration, overriding its actual dialect and configured kind.

anti_pattern.structural_description: A new format reader narrowed previously supported source semantics based on the filename extension.
anti_pattern.why_it_fails: JSON filenames can contain JSONC and can represent registered executable tests.

correct_pattern.required_invariant: Format decoding must preserve configured source ownership and supported annotations.
correct_pattern.implementation_description: Parse JSON/JSONC once, reject duplicate properties, retain comment annotations and parse direct canonical arrays through the existing configured-kind checks.

applicability_conditions: JSON extension dispatch handles both configuration and registered executable sources.
known_non_matches: Host schemas still enforce their own dialect; build-impact remains strict JSON.
confirmation_evidence: The JSONC fixture failed under strict decoding and passes after correction. The actual integrated tsconfig preserves its unit at line 14.
The explicit implementation-only gate rejected configured executable JSON; removing it retains existing kind checks and allows valid integration-test declarations.
regression_proofs: tests/traceability-discovery.test.ts: JSONC configuration preserves existing comment annotations alongside structured declarations
tests/traceability-discovery.test.ts: configured executable JSON preserves test declarations without granting implementation-kind test coverage
